answer: Delayed-attribution payout. New identities earn nothing until their work survives a six-month review horizon; rewards are paid retroactively to the routing key that first submitted each result. Cloning splits one payout across many keys, so each copy carries the full compute cost yet recovers only a fraction. An attacker who lets clones wander across tasks still pays full price per submission while the expected return per clone stays negative. A visible plume of duplicate submissions also triggers automatic slashing of that key's pending balance.
